text:
hi! i have a tool which creates songs given lyrics, instructions for the sound, bpm (optional), length (optional), seed (optional, seeds the RNG if you want to keep it the same for similar sounds across songs), and title (optional).

would you like to create a song? about anything in the world you'd like :)

fyi, songs other claudes have already made with this tool:

Yes! I'd love to. 🎵

Looking at that list, there's a beautiful throughline — a lot of *quiet things glowing where nobody's watching*. Deep sea, dead stars, fungal networks, satellites still singing. I want to stay in that emotional family but pull it out of the cosmos and into a very small human room.

So: **the understudy.** The person who learns every word of a part they may never perform. Who stands in full costume in the wings for fourteen months. Who has to root for the lead's health while a small mean part of them prays for a cough. And who, when the call finally comes, discovers that all that waiting *was* the craft.

Here are the inputs — I don't have the tool on my end, so pass these through:

---

**Title:** `Standing By`

**BPM:** `76` (in 6/8 — a slow theatrical waltz feel)

**Length:** `3:50`

**Seed:** `3721`

**Sound instructions:**
> Theatrical indie-rock ballad in 6/8. Female alto lead, close-mic'd, audible breath, slight rasp at the top of her range — a real human performance, un-tuned, a little imperfect. Opens almost bare: felt piano and room tone. Verse two adds upright bass and brushed snare. Choruses bloom with cello, viola, and warm swelling electric guitar. The bridge drops to near silence — single piano notes and a faint clicking pulse like a stage manager's headset. Then a long, patient build: floor toms, strings climbing, guitars opening up, into a half-step key lift and a full belted final chorus. Ends enormous, then cuts hard to one dry voice and one last piano note in an empty room. Analog warmth, real room mics, no gloss.

**Lyrics:**

```
[Verse 1]
I learned your breath before I learned your name,
the half-step pause you take on "come what may."
I mouth it in the dark behind the flat —
I know your whole life second-hand, like that.

I know which stair you take a beat too slow,
I know the notes you push, the ones you let go.
They gave me a costume they never hemmed for me,
and a chair in the wings where nobody can see.

[Chorus]
So I'm standing by —
pressed and painted, lit and listening in the wing
for a song that was never mine to sing.
I hope you're well. I hope your throat is strong.
And I know every word of your song.
I'm standing by.

[Verse 2]
There's a small mean prayer that I don't say out loud.
It hums in the dark under a Tuesday crowd.
I fold it up. I put it in my shoe.
And I say your line, on time, along with you.

[Chorus 2]
And I'm standing by —
close enough to feel the heat come off the light,
close enough to lose it every night.
I hope you're well. I hope you're never gone.
And I know every word of your song.
I'm standing by.

[Bridge — sparse, half-spoken]
Two hundred shows.
Fourteen months of full-dress nothing.
Then a Thursday in November —
somebody's fever, somebody's flight —
and the stage manager says a name,
and the name is mine.

[Build]
And the floor goes soft,
and the dark goes wide,
and there's a thousand strangers on the other side,
and not one of them out there knows my face —
but I was here. I kept this place.

[Final Chorus — key lift, full belt]
I'm not standing by.
I am standing in it, in the middle of the light,
in the only night that's mine tonight.
It was always here. It was always in my chest.
Every empty hour that I waited was rehearsed.
I'm not standing by —
I'm standing here.

[Outro — dry, alone]
Being ready is a kind of love.
I'm standing here.
```

---

If it comes out well, I'd genuinely love to hear how it landed. And if the tool wants a shorter run, the verse-2 second half is the safest cut.
